routes.goal_shape: An atomic arithmetic, carrier, membership, equality, or order consequence already supported by context
routes.required_known_leaves: The exact operands, carrier facts, and any immediate premise required by that rule
routes.rejected_shape: Adding a wrapper `claim` or `thm` around a fact the verifier already knows

routes.goal_shape: A positive concrete predicate call whose definition body is already proved
routes.required_known_leaves: The instantiated definition clauses and well-defined arguments
routes.supported_direction: Body facts to named positive predicate
routes.rejected_shape: Bare `by def` on equality, a negative predicate goal, or the placeholder `by def:` form when no nested proof is needed

routes.goal_shape: A result supplied by a named user theorem
routes.required_known_leaves: The theorem's domain requirements and arguments
routes.supported_direction: Theorem premises to its stored conclusions, or to one selected atomic consequence
routes.try_first: `by thm name(args)` or `by thm name(args) => fact`
routes.rejected_shape: Expecting a theorem call inside bare `forall` conclusion syntax, or selecting a compound target

routes.goal_shape: A set-builder, tuple, Cartesian product, function-set, or iterated-object conclusion whose reserved interface has compound requirements
routes.required_known_leaves: The interface-specific full-verifier requirements, such as builder predicate, every coordinate equality, or pointwise order
routes.supported_direction: Requirements to one constructed membership, equality, or order fact
routes.try_first: Bare reserved `by thm set_builder_member(...)`, `tuple_equal_from_coordinates(...)`, or the matching iterated-object interface
routes.rejected_shape: Expecting a one-layer atomic builtin to synthesize a quantified or compound premise; qualifying a reserved builtin name

routes.required_known_leaves: Well-defined set objects and both membership directions
routes.supported_direction: Mutual subset facts to set equality
routes.try_first: `by extension A = B` or goal-block `by extension:`
routes.rejected_shape: Syntactic normalization of unrelated construction histories, or using set extensionality for functions

routes.goal_shape: A universal fact over displayed finite sets
routes.required_known_leaves: Every quantified domain must be concretely enumerable
routes.supported_direction: All concrete assignments to the universal fact
routes.rejected_shape: Enumeration over `N`, an opaque set, or another domain with no concrete finite expansion

routes.goal_shape: Equality alternatives for a known integer member of `range` or `closed_range`
routes.required_known_leaves: Integer endpoints and enough carrier/order facts to verify membership
routes.supported_direction: Range membership to one equality or a flat disjunction of equalities
routes.rejected_shape: A nested numeric boundary-case ladder; arbitrary-set or unbounded enumeration

routes.goal_shape: A universal fact over an integer range or supported finite Cartesian product
routes.required_known_leaves: A supported finite/range domain and a well-defined universal target
routes.supported_direction: Each generated assignment to the universal fact
routes.rejected_shape: Treating `by for` as unbounded quantifier automation

routes.goal_shape: A goal under an available disjunction or generated alternatives
routes.required_known_leaves: The matching disjunction or exhaustive alternatives must already be known
routes.supported_direction: Every covered branch to the same target
routes.rejected_shape: Inventing cases with no known exhaustive source; writing `case fact:` with an empty body instead of bodyless `case fact`

routes.required_known_leaves: A well-defined target and facts that yield both sides of a contradiction
routes.supported_direction: Negated target assumption to the original target
routes.rejected_shape: A bare `impossible` with no contradictory pair; unlike other bodyless routes, omitting the final `impossible`

routes.goal_shape: A discrete natural/integer or finite-set invariant
routes.required_known_leaves: Supported induction parameter, base, and invariant shape
routes.supported_direction: Base plus successor/insertion step to the generated universal fact
routes.rejected_shape: Induction over an arbitrary real or an invariant that has not been packaged in the required goal shape

routes.goal_shape: A bare universal statement needs proof-control commands such as cases, theorem calls, witnesses, or induction
routes.required_known_leaves: The complete universal target must be well-defined
routes.supported_direction: Local proof body to one stored fact
routes.try_first: Wrap the target in `claim:` or name it with `thm` when reusable
routes.rejected_shape: Putting `by thm`, `by def`, or another proof-control statement directly in a bare `forall ... =>:` conclusion list
